drivingQuestion: For the view that initial negligence ending in accident is exempt, is damage during birth wholly negligent?

segments.he: אַלִּיבָּא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר תְּחִלָּתוֹ בִּפְשִׁיעָה וְסוֹפוֹ בְּאוֹנֶס חַיָּיב, לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ; כִּי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ – אַלִּיבָּא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר תְּחִלָּתוֹ בִּפְשִׁיעָה וְסוֹפוֹ בְּאוֹנֶס פָּטוּר; מַאי?
segments.en: The Gemara clarifies Rabbi Yirmeya’s question: «Do not raise the dilemma in accordance with» the opinion of «the one who says» that one is «liable» in a case of damage that is «initially through negligence and ultimately by accident,» since in this case the owner was negligent in allowing the animal to enter another person’s courtyard, although the actual causing of the damage was ultimately by accident. «When should you raise this dilemma?» Raise it «in accordance with» the opinion «of the one who says» that one is «exempt» in a case that is «initially through negligence and ultimately by accident. What» is the halakha in this case?

segments.he: מִי אָמְרִינַן: כֵּיוָן דִּתְחִלָּתוֹ בִּפְשִׁיעָה וְסוֹפוֹ בְּאוֹנֶס – פָּטוּר; אוֹ דִלְמָא, הָכָא כּוּלַּהּ בִּפְשִׁיעָה הוּא – דְּכֵיוָן דְּקָא חָזֵי דִּקְרִיבָה לַהּ לְמֵילַד, אִיבְּעִי לֵיהּ לְנָטוֹרַהּ
segments.en: The two sides of the question are as follows: «Do we say» that, «since» this case is «initially through negligence and ultimately by accident,» he is «exempt» from liability? «Or perhaps here,» in this case, «it is entirely» due to his «negligence; since he saw that» the animal «was close to giving birth, he should have safeguarded it» adequately
«and taken care of it,» and he bears responsibility for failing to do so. The dilemma «shall stand» unresolved.
